Maya: Hitting a weird KV-cache correctness issue after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout (v2). Memory climbs slowly on long-context workloads and some responses include garbage tokens that look like cross-request contamination. :confused:
Sam: @Maya can you paste a minimal repro + which flag rolled out?
Maya: Repro steps in a sec. Running with --batch-heuristic=adaptive --kernel-selector=v2 on dedicated GPUs. Sequence mixes: long (30k) followed by short (128) requests. Snippet of the request config:
```json
{ "model": "open-xxl", "seq_len": 30000, "batching": "on" }
```
Logs show repeated warnings like:```WARN kvcache: page_offset_mismatch page_id=42 expected=128 actual=136 seq=2045```
InfraBot: deploy/rollout completed: kernel-selector=v2 on eng-runtime-dedicated-1 @2026-02-12T03:21Z :white_check_mark:
Liam: I saw memory drift before but chalked it up to eviction delay. Do the corrupted responses always follow a long->short transition?
Maya: Yes, pattern is long then short. Short requests sometimes pick up stale KV blocks at wrong token alignment and produce suffixes from previous long request. Also see slow mem growth over many cycles. :bug:
Anya: Can you enable debug kv headers and drop a page dump? Try KV_DEBUG=1 and reproduce, then attach /tmp/kv-dump.log.
Maya: Did that. Header dump shows snippets like:
```
KVPAGE hdr: id=0x7f2a size=4096 start_token=128 align=16 tag=0x12 prev_req=1023
... later ...
KVPAGE hdr: id=0x7f2a size=4096 start_token=136 align=16 tag=0x12 prev_req=2045
```
Same tag but prev_req changed and start_token shifted by 8 without eviction record. Looks like reuse without proper reinitialization.
Sam: Interesting. Kernel-selector v2 might be switching tile/granularity (GEMM tiling) which changes how we compute token-aligned offsets. If allocator assumed pre-v2 tile=8, but v2 uses tile=16/32, index arithmetic could be off when recycled pages were laid out under different assumptions.
Liam: I also noticed kernel v2 sets tile=32 default in the selection path. That would change offset normalization. Check kv_indexer and allocator normalization path for tile/granularity coupling.
Maya: I threw an assertion in the runtime: `assert(page.start_token % tile == 0)` and it fired intermittently when switching kernels mid-workload.
Sam: Quick mitigation: on reuse, allocator should normalize start_token to the current tile and zero the page header to avoid stale prev_req metadata. Longer term the kernel selector should advertise granularity to the allocator or we keep a per-page granularity tag.
Anya: There's also a race: async eviction can run concurrently with a batch finish. If eviction frees a page and it gets reassigned while the kernel selection path changes tiling, we might see misaligned reuse. Add extra synchronization or zero-on-alloc as defense.
Maya: Repro script I'm running:```bash
# reproduce locally
KV_DEBUG=1 ./run_serving --kernel-selector=v2 --batch-heuristic=adaptive --seed=42 &
# send mixed seq lengths: 30000 then 128 repeated
```
Sam: Good repro. I'll draft a hotfix: (1) zero page header on allocate, (2) normalize start_token = (start_token / tile) * tile on reuse, (3) add assertion in tests. Can you attach the kv-dump log path?
Maya: Logs are at /tmp/kv-2860001234-dump.log and I pushed a small reproducer to gist: https://gist.github.com/example/kv-repro (private).
Liam: I'll add a unit test that simulates interleaved seq lengths and kernel tile flips to ensure no cross-request contamination. Also will add a check that prev_req is only valid if page was zeroed since last allocation.
Sam: I'll open PR with allocator normalization + extra zeroing and a short-term runtime guard. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:
InfraBot: CI triggered: jobs/eng-runtime/kv-fix-run (#12345) started.
Maya: Thanks all. Leaving additional context in the reproducer and dump. Ping me if you need packet captures or perf traces. :eyes:
